# PPL Hypertrophy Tracker — Full Knowledge Base & Technical Specification

> PPL Hypertrophy Tracker is an evidence-based progressive overload workout web application, biomechanical training operating system, and peer-reviewed resistance sports science journal published at https://ppltracker.web.id.

- Domain: https://ppltracker.web.id
- Source Repository: https://github.com/farhanazeemi/ppl-tracker
- Tech Stack: Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Supabase PostgreSQL with RLS, Sanity Studio CMS
- License: MIT Open Access
- Contact: farhanazeemi.dev@gmail.com

---

## 1. Core Platform Architecture

PPL Hypertrophy Tracker is built as a zero-latency, local-first progressive web application (PWA) with cloud synchronization via Supabase PostgreSQL. 

### Local-First Persistence
The application operates fully offline in the gym:
- Working sets, reps, load, and completion states are continuously synchronized to localStorage (`ppl_sets_v2`, `ppl_history_v2`).
- When network connectivity is present, authenticated users automatically synchronize workout logs and profile biometrics to Supabase with Row Level Security (RLS).
- Guest mode lifters maintain 100% functionality locally without mandatory account creation.

### Biomechanical Visualization & Rest Audio
- Web Audio API synthesizes millisecond-accurate acoustic frequency beeps at 3s, 2s, 1s, and completion (880Hz / 1760Hz sine bursts), functioning even when the device is locked or in background mode via timestamp differential tracking.
- Interactive 3D muscle anatomy visualizer highlights primary agonist and secondary synergist muscles for all programmed exercises.

---

## 2. Periodized Training Splits & Full Exercise Database

The platform natively supports 4 periodized training splits:

### Split 1: 6-Day Push • Pull • Legs (PPL)
Optimal for intermediate to advanced lifters aiming to stimulate muscle groups twice every 7–8 days with 10–20 weekly sets per muscle group.

#### Push A (Upper Chest & Anterior Delt Focus)
1. Low Incline Dumbbell Press — Clavicular Pectoralis Major (3 sets x 8–10 reps, 120s rest)
2. Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press — Anterior & Lateral Deltoids (3 sets x 8–12 reps, 120s rest)
3. Flat Machine Chest Press / Converging Press — Sternal Pectoralis Major (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
4. Dumbbell / Cable Lateral Raises — Lateral Deltoids (4 sets x 12–15 reps, 60s rest)
5. Overhead Cable Rope Triceps Extension — Triceps Long Head (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
6. Triceps Rope Pushdown — Triceps Lateral & Medial Heads (3 sets x 12–15 reps, 60s rest)

#### Pull A (Lat Width & Upper Back Thickness)
1. Lat Pulldown / Neutral Grip Pulldown — Latissimus Dorsi (3 sets x 8–10 reps, 120s rest)
2. Chest-Supported T-Bar / Machine Row — Mid Trapezius & Rhomboids (3 sets x 8–12 reps, 120s rest)
3. Seated Cable Row (Close-Grip) — Lower Lats & Spinal Erectors (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
4. Incline Dumbbell Bicep Curl — Biceps Brachii Long Head (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
5. Standing Hammer Curl — Brachialis & Brachioradialis (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 60s rest)
6. Cable Face Pull — Rear Deltoids & External Rotators (3 sets x 15–20 reps, 60s rest)

#### Legs A (Quad Dominant & Calves)
1. Barbell Back Squat / Hack Squat — Quadriceps & Gluteus Maximus (3 sets x 6–8 reps, 180s rest)
2. Romanian Deadlift (RDL) — Hamstrings & Glutes in Lengthened Position (3 sets x 8–10 reps, 180s rest)
3. Leg Press / Belt Squat — Quadriceps (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 120s rest)
4. Seated Leg Curl — Hamstrings Biceps Femoris (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
5. Standing Calf Raise — Gastrocnemius (4 sets x 12–15 reps, 60s rest)

#### Push B (Shoulders & Triceps Overload with Chest Maintenance)
1. Standing / Seated Overhead Barbell Press — Anterior Deltoid & Triceps (3 sets x 6–8 reps, 180s rest)
2. Incline Machine Chest Press — Upper Pectoralis (3 sets x 8–10 reps, 120s rest)
3. Pec Deck Fly / Cable Crossover — Pectoralis Sternal in Shortened Contraction (3 sets x 12–15 reps, 90s rest)
4. Lean-Away Cable Lateral Raise — Lateral Deltoid (4 sets x 12–15 reps, 60s rest)
5. Barbell / EZ-Bar Skull Crusher — Triceps Brachii (3 sets x 8–10 reps, 90s rest)
6. Cable Dual Rope Kickback — Triceps Long Head (3 sets x 12–15 reps, 60s rest)

#### Pull B (Upper Back & Rear Delts Focus)
1. Barbell Bent-Over Row / Pendlay Row — Latissimus & Trapezius (3 sets x 6–8 reps, 180s rest)
2. Single-Arm High Cable Lat Row — Illiac Lat Fiber Bias (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
3. Chest-Supported Incline DB Row — Rear Deltoids & Rhomboids (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
4. Bayesian Cable Curl — Biceps Brachii Lengthened Position (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
5. Preacher Curl (Dumbbell or Machine) — Biceps Brachii Shortened Position (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 60s rest)
6. Reverse Pec Deck / Rear Delt Fly — Posterior Deltoid (4 sets x 12–15 reps, 60s rest)

#### Legs B (Posterior Chain & Hamstring Focus)
1. Conventional Deadlift / Trap Bar Deadlift — Entire Posterior Chain (3 sets x 5–6 reps, 180s rest)
2. Bulgarian Split Squat — Quads & Gluteus Medius / Maximus (3 sets x 8–10 reps/leg, 120s rest)
3. Lying Hamstring Curl — Knee Flexion Hamstrings (3 sets x 10–12 reps, 90s rest)
4. Leg Extension — Rectus Femoris & Vastus Lateralis (3 sets x 12–15 reps, 90s rest)
5. Seated Calf Raise — Soleus (4 sets x 12–15 reps, 60s rest)

---

### Split 2: 4-Day Upper / Lower
Designed for balanced recovery, 4 days per week:
- Day 1: Upper Body A (Heavy Horizontal Press & Vertical Pull)
- Day 2: Lower Body A (Squat Dominant & Leg Curl)
- Day 3: Rest / Active Recovery
- Day 4: Upper Body B (Overhead Press & Horizontal Row)
- Day 5: Lower Body B (Hinge / Deadlift Dominant & Quad Extensions)
- Days 6–7: Rest

---

### Split 3: 5-Day Bro Split
Classic bodybuilder specialization split hitting one major muscle group daily with concentrated volume:
- Day 1: Chest & Core
- Day 2: Back & Lats
- Day 3: Shoulders & Traps
- Day 4: Legs & Calves
- Day 5: Arms (Biceps & Triceps Super-sets)
- Days 6–7: Rest

---

### Split 4: 3-Day Full Body
High-frequency stimulus ideal for beginner/intermediate athletes or time-constrained schedules:
- Day 1: Full Body A (Squat, Bench Press, Barbell Row, Bicep Curl, Calves)
- Day 2: Rest
- Day 3: Full Body B (Deadlift, Overhead Press, Lat Pulldown, Tricep Pushdown, Core)
- Day 4: Rest
- Day 5: Full Body C (Leg Press, Incline DB Press, Cable Row, Lateral Raise, Hamstring Curl)
- Days 6–7: Rest

---

## 3. Double Progression Algorithm

The double progression model is a mathematical, auto-regulated method to systematically guarantee progressive tension overload without sacrificing biomechanical execution:

### Algorithm Specification:
1. Every exercise is assigned a lower repetition floor ($R_{min}$) and an upper repetition ceiling ($R_{max}$), typically 8–12 reps for compound movements and 10–15 reps for isolation movements.
2. The lifter begins at load $W_0$.
3. When performing set $S_i$ of $N$ prescribed working sets:
   - If the lifter records reps $R_i \ge R_{max}$ across **ALL** sets $S_1, S_2, \dots, S_N$ at load $W_0$, the system triggers an overload breakthrough event.
   - The user is instructed to advance working load:
     $$W_{next} = W_0 + \Delta W$$
     where $\Delta W$ is the minimum plate increment: $+2.5\text{ kg}$ ($+5\text{ lbs}$) for upper body compounds, or $+5\text{ kg}$ ($+10\text{ lbs}$) for lower body compounds.
   - For the subsequent workout session, the target reps reset to $R_{min}$ at the new load $W_{next}$.
4. If any set falls short of $R_{max}$, the lifter remains at load $W_0$ in the next session, focusing on accumulating additional repetitions before advancing weight.

---

## 4. Olympic Barbell Plate Calculator Mathematics

The visual barbell calculator computes symmetric plate distribution per side for Olympic standard barbells:

### Specifications:
- Default Barbell Weight: $W_{bar} = 20\text{ kg}$ ($45\text{ lbs}$) for men's standard Olympic bar; $15\text{ kg}$ ($35\text{ lbs}$) for women's standard Olympic bar.
- Available Plate Denominations (per side):
  - Metric (kg): $[25, 20, 15, 10, 5, 2.5, 1.25]$
  - Imperial (lbs): $[45, 35, 25, 10, 5, 2.5]$
- Plate Calculation Formula:
  $$W_{side} = \frac{W_{total} - W_{bar}}{2}$$
  Greedy algorithm distributes plates from largest denomination to smallest. Any residual $W_{rem} < 1.25\text{ kg}$ ($< 2.5\text{ lbs}$) is flagged with precision tolerance warnings.

---

## 5. Exercise Substitution Intelligence

The Workout Substitution Finder (/tools/workout-substitution-finder) matches replacement exercises using 3 biomechanical vectors:
1. **Target Muscle Group & Anatomical Subdivision**: e.g., Clavicular Pectoralis Major vs Sternal Pectoralis Major; Latissimus Dorsi Iliac vs Thoracic fibers.
2. **Resistance Profile Curve**: Lengthened position peak resistance (e.g., Dumbbell RDL, Bayesian Curl, Incline DB Press) vs Shortened position peak resistance (e.g., Cable Crossover, Preacher Curl, Leg Extension).
3. **Equipment Availability & Joint Comfort**: Barbell, Dumbbell, Cable, Machine, Smith Machine, or Bodyweight.
